# SOC-C13 extraction notes (A2, prompt v3)

## Rows proposed
- findings: 49 (N 31, Q 18). transformations: 4 (2 cross strand: F6, F16; 2 cost models N to N: F48, F49). claims: 73. relations: 29 (backs 20, covers 9, clashes 0). decisions: header only.
- Headline scope: executive summary (p.9-15, including its Discussion and conclusions and Recommendations) and Chapter 6 Implications and Recommendations (p.65-68). The recommendations on p.14-15 and p.67-68 are the same text; each is one row with both locations (rule 11). Section "Concluding comments" inside Chapter 4 (p.31, p.43, p.45, p.49, p.61) were not treated as headline locations but used under rule 7.

## Look at first
1. Joint claims (direct rests_on in both strands): C9, C10, C11, C22, C34, C40. Transformations do not add any (F6 and F16 have Q roots only; F48, F49 are N to N).
   - C34 (adult workers particularly important / crucial / main engine): rests on Table 5 (F35, p.11 "Quantitative analysis found") and the case studies (F36, F37, p.12 "To explore this further", p.13 "First... Second..."). Fit proposed confirm; expand is defensible, since the case studies add the mechanism (risk thinking).
   - C40 (adult workers linked to reduced need for care): the link is explicit on p.45 ("This might go some way to explaining the reduction in children entering care"), so F37 is in rests_on with F34 (days in care) and F35. A1 may judge F34 a premise rather than support.
   - C22 (conditions put in place swiftly, practice changes take time): p.13 rests on F28; p.65 adds "our qualitative evidence suggested that initial enthusiasm had been created through the training in MI [...] and the group discussions showed evidence of producing more reflective and thoughtful consideration of cases". A2 mapped this to F4 and F38; the MI "qualitative evidence" has no exact matching finding (F10, survey, is the nearest quantitative one). Weakest of the joint claims.
   - C9 rests on F1 (interviews) and F8, F9 (survey) because p.27 states survey findings "were consistent with interview findings" and the p.31 conclusion merges both ("the picture painted by staff is positive"). Fit confirm.
   - C10 and C11 rest on office-level survey data (F18) and the account of working context (F19, p.31). The source of F19 is not stated (probably interviews and fieldwork); A1 should confirm it is a Q finding. C11 also uses F13 (open-ended: access to adult workers) and F16 (count of caseload comments).
2. Relation R8 (C37 backs C36): the only cross-strand corroboration stated at claim level ("This encouraging picture was also reflected in qualitative feedback from families and social workers", p.11). The text names no specific qualitative findings; A2 assigned F2, F7, F14, F30 to C37.
3. R9 (C38 backs C39) rests on "It seems clear that" after the case-study sentence; the marker is weaker than "therefore" (rule 10).
4. Discrepancies between executive summary and results:
   - C12: executive summary gives domestic abuse 44%; results give 53% domestic violence (p.32); 44% is housing problems.
   - C35: "an average positive change of 6 points" is not reported; Table 5 gives +7.00, +5.56, +6.25 (and +3.60 for perpetrator workers) against +3.3 to +3.75 without.
   - C31: reduction in days in care (20.54 to 9.81) is not statistically significant (p=0.06, p.40); the executive summary does not say so, and p.43 says "There can be no doubt that FSH reduced the use of care". The cost model (Table 30) uses a 39% reduction from a separate child-level HCC analysis.
   - C48: "reduced by one-half on average" corresponds to the projected 53% (Table 31); observed cohort reductions are 31%, 53% and 100% (Table 26).
   - C50: £2.6 million vs Table 13 total £2,671,260 and p.60 "over £2.5 million". Police saving printed as £106,284 on p.95 vs £106,824 in Table 32.
5. Possible tension, not proposed as clash (rule 4): C45 (KPIs give "limited evidence to evaluate FSH as a reform") and C66 ("unequivocal support for continuing the development of FSH"). Both can hold, since C66 concerns continuation and rests on several sources.

## Design-level interface points (rules 9, 13; not transformations)
- Coded observations (p.35-36): audio-recorded meetings rated on 7 MITI-derived dimensions, reduced by a factor analysis on another sample to "care and engagement" and "good authority". Scores are built from observed interaction, but no qualitative finding from the recordings is reported, so F25-F28 are N roots. A1 may wish to treat this as an instrument (rule 9).
- Case studies (p.43-44): selected after the Table 5 result ("A hypothesis we developed from this data [...] To explore these 2 ideas we collected some specific sources of information"); 5 families chosen from the comparative dataset by criteria, 5 nominated by staff; they "combined qualitative and quantitative data" per family, but reported results are narrative (F36, F37, Q). The selection is not a comparison of qualitative data across quantitatively defined groups, so rule 12 was not applied.
- Qualitative coding frame built by concept mapping from interview questions (p.72).
- Office-level account (p.30-31): survey differences between offices are explained with qualitative context. The offices are not groups defined by a quantitative measure, so this was not recorded as a rule 12 transformation; flagged for A1.

## Rule 3 notes (findings bearing on a claim but not linked by the text)
- C6 (case discussions positive): the executive summary says "qualitative feedback"; survey F11 (>80% better risk understanding, but 58% not an effective use of time) is not used.
- C7 and C72 (workbooks): F12 (survey, 30% unable to use the workbook) not used; C72 cites no findings and the structured Intervention Programme has no finding.
- C8 (energy, commitment): F8 (three-quarters excited) and F19 ("feel-good factor [...] was palpable") are thematically close; not linked (rule 8 not met).
- C54 (informal discussions): only a staff quote on p.27 ("informal catch ups over coffee", in F7); not linked.
- C60 (variation in integration of adult workers): F2 (variation between offices) and F13 (access) not linked.
- C63 (next phase of training): F10 (one-half report sufficient MI support) not linked.
- C24 ("some significant shifts"): left empty; may refer to F27 or to outcome findings.
- C32 (children returning from care more quickly): no supporting finding in the text.

## Other choices
- C27-C29 split per outcome (rule 1) from one executive-summary sentence.
- C1 merges the p.9-10 "huge amount was achieved" with p.12 "depth and breadth [...] exceptional" (rule 11); A1 may prefer two rows.
- C18 rests on F26 and F27 by rule 8 (small improvement restates the t-test results).
- Evaluative sentences not registered: "This is an important positive finding in relation to FSH" (p.11, about C31); "Our pattern of findings is best explained by 2 crucial lessons" (p.65, framing).
- Research-agenda content (p.62-64, future evaluation) excluded under rule 6.
- F20 relies on Figure 1, which is an image; the caseload values are not in the extracted text.
